articles.title: The Topics Seasonality Model
articles.abstract: Does the timing of the world's curiosity keep time with the sky? We fit 22 years of MONTHLY Google-Trends interest for 2149 search fields (skill terms derived from ISCO-08 occupations, plus learning topics) to eleven sidereal bodies — each a parameter-free SINC of its angular distance Δ to a shared phase, at a resonance PERIOD tuned per keyword (reported in years) to maximise F1 of the fit R² and the sign decisiveness. Bodies' own periods are measured day-by-day from the ephemeris — with exactly one non-negative weight per body and NO intercept (11 parameters), the shared phase swept on a 5° grid to place each field's zodiac sign. The median in-sample R² is carried mostly by the slow outer bodies acting as a trend basis plus the Sun's annual term: drop the slow bodies and it collapses. A transparent least-squares re-description of trend and seasonality, not a claim of cause.

articles.title: Google Trends Recency Bias
articles.abstract: How much recent Google-Trends data should a model ignore? We crop the recent tail of each MONTHLY series and refit, sweeping 0 to 6 years, and score each crop by pure in-sample R² — no hold-out. Fitting power climbs as the noisy recent year is dropped, knees within roughly the first year, then falls as too much history is discarded — so the model crops one year.
